  • Method Details

    • deviceVerificationPage

      @RequestMapping(method=GET, value="/oauth2/device_verification", produces="text/html") org.springframework.http.ResponseEntity<String> deviceVerificationPage(@Size(max=32) @Valid @RequestParam(value="user_code",required=false) @Nullable @Size(max=32) @Valid String userCode, @Valid @RequestParam(value="error",required=false) @Nullable @Valid String error, @Valid @RequestParam(value="success",required=false) @Nullable @Valid String success)
      GET /oauth2/device_verification : Renders the device verification page Renders the page the verification URI of the device authorization response points to: the form where the user types the code the device displays (RFC 8628). The form posts the code to the authorization server's own device verification endpoint (POST /oauth2/device_verification, owned by the framework, with the CSRF token), never to this operation. A request that already carries the code (verification_uri_complete) is answered by that endpoint directly, which also applies the multi-factor policy of the account and the limit on the attempts, and sends the browser on to the consent page (GET /oauth2/consent) or back here with a confirmation or an error. A request without a signed-in session is redirected to the sign-in page and resumed afterwards.
      Parameters:
      userCode - A user code to prefill in the form. Any value that is not a plausible code is ignored. (optional)
      error - Present (its value is ignored, usually empty) when the previous attempt failed; the page then shows a message that never says why (an unknown, expired or already used code look the same). (optional)
      success - Present (its value is ignored, usually empty) when the user has just approved the device; the page then says that the device may continue. (optional)
      Returns:
      The device verification page. (status code 200)
